### Problem: label edges so the largest path MEX is small {#sec-tr-p5-mex}

::: {.p-statement}
Label the $n - 1$ edges with $0, 1, \ldots, n - 2$, each once. For a pair of vertices, the MEX of the path is the smallest missing non-negative label on it. Minimise the largest of these MEXes, and print one label per edge in input order. Any optimal labelling is accepted.

Constraints: $2 \le n \le 10^5$.

Source: [CF 1325C · Ehab and Path-etic MEXs](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1325/C){.solved rating="1500"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
On a path, some pair's route is the whole tree, so the largest MEX is $n - 1$ no matter how you label. If some vertex has degree at least $3$, three edges meet there. Put $0, 1, 2$ on three of them. Every path misses at least one of those three, because a path uses at most two edges at a vertex. The largest MEX is then $2$. For $n \ge 3$ the labels $0$ and $1$ lie on some common path, so some MEX is at least $2$, and the three labels at one vertex meet that bound.
:::

::: {#fig-tr-mex}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):

    root = V.Node("2", [
        V.Node("1", [V.Node("3", edge="3")], edge="0", color="green"),
        V.Node("4", edge="1"),
        V.Node("5", [V.Node("6", edge="4")], edge="2"),
    ], color="green")
    V.tree(ax, p, root, dx=1.25, dy=1.35, size=10)

V.show(draw)
```

One optimal labelling of the sample. The labels $0, 1, 2$ all touch vertex $2$. A path uses at most two of them, so every path MEX is at most $2$.

:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **At a hub.** If any vertex has degree $\ge 3$, write $0, 1, 2$ on the first three of its edges in input order, and write the remaining labels on the remaining edges.
2. **On leaf edges.** The same three labels on three edges that touch a leaf. A tree with a vertex of degree $\ge 3$ has at least three leaves, so three leaf edges exist. A path has two leaves; the labels may sit anywhere and the largest MEX is $n - 1$.

**Invariant.** Labels are a permutation of $0..n-2$, because each edge is written once. When a hub exists, no path contains all three of $0, 1, 2$.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### At a hub

::: {.form-next}
The last vertex of degree at least $3$ is enough. There is nothing to search: three edges at one vertex already force the bound.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get('mex', 'hub')
    assert str(final) == '2'
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def ehab_at_hub(n, edges):
    deg = [0] * (n + 1)
    for u, v in edges:
        deg[u] += 1
        deg[v] += 1
    hub = next((x for x in range(n, 0, -1) if deg[x] >= 3), None)
    label = [-1] * (n - 1)
    nxt = 0
    if hub is not None:
        for i, (u, v) in enumerate(edges):
            if nxt >= 3:
                break
            if u == hub or v == hub:
                label[i] = nxt
                nxt += 1
    for i in range(n - 1):
        if label[i] == -1:
            label[i] = nxt
            nxt += 1
    return label
```

##### C++

```cpp
vector<int> ehabAtHub(int n, const vector<pair<int, int>>& edges) {
    vector<int> deg(n + 1), label(n - 1, -1);
    for (auto [u, v] : edges) ++deg[u], ++deg[v];
    int hub = -1;
    for (int x = 1; x <= n; ++x) if (deg[x] >= 3) hub = x;
    int nxt = 0;
    if (hub != -1) {
        for (int i = 0; i < n - 1 && nxt < 3; ++i)
            if (edges[i].first == hub || edges[i].second == hub)
                label[i] = nxt++;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; ++i)
        if (label[i] == -1) label[i] = nxt++;
    return label;
}
```

:::

#### On leaf edges

::: {.form-next}
Put $0, 1, 2$ on the first three leaf edges instead of on the hub. The largest MEX is the same. A path skips this and just numbers the edges in order.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get('mex', 'leaf')
    assert str(final) == '2'
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def ehab_at_leaves(n, edges):
    deg = [0] * (n + 1)
    for u, v in edges:
        deg[u] += 1
        deg[v] += 1
    leaves = sum(1 for x in range(1, n + 1) if deg[x] == 1)
    label = [-1] * (n - 1)
    nxt = 0
    if leaves >= 3:
        for i, (u, v) in enumerate(edges):
            if nxt >= 3:
                break
            if deg[u] == 1 or deg[v] == 1:
                label[i] = nxt
                nxt += 1
    for i in range(n - 1):
        if label[i] == -1:
            label[i] = nxt
            nxt += 1
    return label


def largest_mex(n, edges, label):
    """Largest path MEX. Labels are small on the trees this checks."""
    adj = [[] for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for i, (u, v) in enumerate(edges):
        adj[u].append((v, label[i]))
        adj[v].append((u, label[i]))
    best = 0
    for s in range(1, n + 1):
        st = [(s, -1, 0)]
        while st:
            u, parent, mask = st.pop()
            for v, lab in adj[u]:
                if v == parent:
                    continue
                nm = mask | (1 << lab)
                mex = 0
                while nm & (1 << mex):
                    mex += 1
                best = max(best, mex)
                st.append((v, u, nm))
    return best


edges = [(1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 4), (2, 5), (5, 6)]
assert sorted(ehab_at_hub(6, edges)) == list(range(5))
assert largest_mex(6, edges, ehab_at_hub(6, edges)) == 2
assert largest_mex(6, edges, ehab_at_leaves(6, edges)) == 2
path = [(i, i + 1) for i in range(1, 4)]
assert largest_mex(4, path, ehab_at_hub(4, path)) == 3
assert ehab_at_hub(2, [(1, 2)]) == [0]
```

##### C++

```cpp
vector<int> ehabAtLeaves(int n, const vector<pair<int, int>>& edges) {
    vector<int> deg(n + 1), label(n - 1, -1);
    for (auto [u, v] : edges) ++deg[u], ++deg[v];
    int leaves = 0;
    for (int x = 1; x <= n; ++x) leaves += deg[x] == 1;
    int nxt = 0;
    if (leaves >= 3) {
        for (int i = 0; i < n - 1 && nxt < 3; ++i)
            if (deg[edges[i].first] == 1 || deg[edges[i].second] == 1)
                label[i] = nxt++;
    }
    for (int i = 0; i < n - 1; ++i)
        if (label[i] == -1) label[i] = nxt++;
    return label;
}
```

:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
$O(n)$ time and memory. The largest MEX is $2$ when a vertex of degree $\ge 3$ exists, and $n - 1$ when the tree is a path (or a single edge, where it is $1$).
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- $n = 2$: one edge, label $0$, largest MEX $1$.
- $n = 3$, two edges from vertex $1$: labels $0, 1$, largest MEX $2$. There is no vertex of degree $3$; the two-edge path is the whole tree.
- Sample edges `1-2, 1-3, 2-4, 2-5, 5-6` have a hub at $2$. One optimal labelling is `0 3 1 2 4`. The official sample line may differ. Both have largest MEX $2$. Diffing your line against the sample rejects a correct answer.
- Putting $0$ and $1$ at the hub and $2$ somewhere else lets a path pick up all three. The MEX becomes $3$.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Labels written in DFS order land on the wrong edges. The array is indexed by the input position.
- Putting $0$ and $1$ on the hub and $2$ somewhere else lets one path collect all three, and the MEX becomes $3$.
- The official sample line is one labelling among many. A diff against that line rejects correct answers.
:::

**Variants.** The number alone, with no labelling printed, is $2$ when some degree is at least $3$, and $n - 1$ on a path. Prime weights on paths of one or two edges are [CF 1627C · Not Assigning](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1627/C){rating="1400"}. Distinct colours on the edges at each vertex are [AC abc146_d · Coloring Edges on Tree](https://atcoder.jp/contests/abc146/tasks/abc146_d).
